hint.label: Vocabulary

flip.text:
1954
Racial segregation in schools is declared unconstitutional.

1955
Montgomery bus boycott: No African Americans take public buses for almost a year, after Rosa Parks' arrest for refusing to let a white passenger have her seat.

1963
March on Washington: Martin Luther King Jr., one of the leaders of the Civil Rights Movement, delivers the speech “I Have a Dream” during the March.

1964
The Civil Rights Act aims to outlaw discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, or nationality.

flip.text:
2008
Barack Obama, a democratic senator, becomes the first Black President of the United States.

2013 onwards
Black Lives Matter campaign is initiated on social media platforms and evolves into a worldwide protest movement, addressing issues of racially motivated police brutality. It is seen as a renewal of the Civil Rights Movement.

2020
George Floyd, a Black man, is murdered by a white police officer in public, kneeling on his neck. This led to a major protest movement in the US.
